terms.grammar: relative adverb, with the indicative; answered by tamdiū
evidence: Sen. Ep. 76.3: tamdiū discendum est quamdiū nesciās
terms.comment: The two actions last the same time.

evidence: Plaut. Persa 113: Dum māne est, omnīs ēsse mortālīs decet.
Ov. Met. 2.89: dum rēsque sinit, tua corrige vōta
terms.comment: For the shorter “while”, during which something else happens, see while.

evidence: Cic. Att. 15.23.1: quoad erit integrum (Lewis & Short)
Ov. Tr. 1.9.5: dōnec eris sōspes, multōs numerābis amīcōs
terms.comment: In this sense ante-classical, poetic and post-Augustan; Cicero has dōnec only for “until” (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: tamdiū discendum est quamdiū nesciās; sī prōverbiō crēdimus, quamdiū vīvās
phrases.english: one must learn as long as one does not know; and, if we believe the proverb, as long as one lives

phrases.latin: Dum māne est, omnīs ēsse mortālīs decet.
phrases.english: As long as it is morning, every mortal ought to eat.

phrases.latin: nāte, cavē, dum rēsque sinit, tua corrige vōta
phrases.english: take care, my son, and change your wish while there is still time

phrases.latin: dōnec eris sōspes, multōs numerābis amīcōs
phrases.english: as long as you do well, you will count many friends
